partially_covered.missing: Organization information is still limited to address and identifier; no properties for organization name, contact details, or legal metadata. No explicit class for organization contact or communication details.
Item information remains limited to name and description. No properties for item codes, units of measure, product category, or classification. No linkage to EN 16931-1 or P2P-O item codes.

Validation rules and SHACL constraints are structurally present, but mandatory fields per EDIFACT D96A directory are still not explicitly modeled or enforced. No SHACL shapes or OWL restrictions for required elements.

cq_coverage.details: Most CQs about invoice structure, roles, line items, and amounts are well covered. Metadata for organizations and items, and explicit validation of mandatory fields, remain incomplete. No major progress on CQ5, CQ8, or CQ13 since last iteration.

strengths: Deep and rich hierarchy for EDIFACT structures and roles
Good use of property characteristics (functional, inverses)
Advanced constructs with owl:equivalentClass and restrictions
weaknesses: Limited coverage of organization and item metadata
Disjointness could be further refined for technical elements

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4 (Missing domain or range for some properties)
P7 (Potentially missing annotation values in edge cases)
reasoner_risks: Hermit may struggle with deep inverse chains and complex restrictions if extended
No datatype violations detected; should be reasoner-safe

suggestions_ignored: Expand organization metadata: add properties for organization name, contact info, and legal identifiers. Model mandatory fields for D96A directory explicitly and enforce via SHACL constraints.
Add general class axioms (GCAs) to define complex business logic, e.g., for validating that sum of invoice lines matches invoice amount. Use owl:hasKey for reference numbers.
Expand item modeling: add item codes, units of measure, and classification properties (e.g., product category).
Add EDIFACT segment code mappings and technical annotations for segments and elements (e.g., BGM, NAD, LIN).
improvement_tracking.notes: No substantive changes since last iteration. Previous improvement suggestions were not implemented. Coverage and quality scores remain unchanged. No new issues introduced; the ontology is stable but missing key enrichments for full CQ coverage and technical depth.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand organization metadata: add properties for organization name, contact info (e.g., email, phone), and legal identifiers. Create an OrganizationContact class if needed. Enrich Address with contact details.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Full coverage for CQ5, improved interoperability for procurement use cases.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Explicitly model mandatory EDIFACT D96A fields (e.g., invoice date, buyer/seller identifier) and enforce presence via SHACL constraints or OWL restrictions.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Full coverage for CQ13, robust validation, and technical compliance.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand item modeling: add item codes, units of measure, product classification/category, and link to external standards (EN 16931-1, P2P-O).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improved coverage for CQ8 and support for industrial procurement scenarios.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add general class axioms (GCAs) to define business logic, such as sum of invoice line net prices equals invoice amount. Use owl:hasKey for reference numbers.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Richer axiomatization and better automated validation.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add EDIFACT segment code mappings and technical annotations for segments and elements (e.g., BGM, NAD, LIN), including code properties and technical notes.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Better alignment with EDIFACT and easier technical integration.

summary: The ontology remains structurally strong and OWL 2 compliant, with no new technical issues. However, none of the previous improvement suggestions were implemented; organization and item metadata and mandatory field validation are still missing, limiting full CQ coverage and technical depth. Progress is fair, but further enrichment is needed for a production-grade model.
